scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

Here are a few reasons why a suit and tie might make you feel that way:

| Why it works | What it does |

| **Physical fit** | A well‑fitted suit can feel comfortable and supportive, reducing distractions and letting you focus on the task at hand. |
| **Self‑image** | Seeing yourself in a polished outfit can reinforce a positive self‑image, which in turn boosts confidence. |

If you’re looking to extend that confidence into other areas, you might try:

1. **Pair it with a personal mantra** – a short phrase you repeat before stepping out the door (e.g., “I’m prepared and capable”).  
2. **Practice power poses** – standing tall for a minute before a big event can reinforce that confident feeling.  
3. **Keep a “confidence journal”** – jot down moments when the suit helped you feel empowered; over time you’ll see patterns and reinforce the habit.
